brief.situation: You are the ML engineer at Parcelo, a fictional delivery company. The ETA model serves every delivery estimate. At 15:50 Model Monitoring raised a training-serving skew alert on the feature trip_distance. Customer complaints say ETAs are far too short. Mobile app 5.2 rolled out to most drivers this afternoon. The evening rush, 40% of daily orders, starts at 17:00.
handover: The model was trained on trip_distance in kilometers.
The data science lead suggests 'just retrain on the last week of data'.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the driver app versions, the feature they send and the model's training distribution.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: what the skew alert meant, what you changed, and why not retrain.

parts.label: Meant
parts.modelAnswer: Only app 5.2's trip_distance was low by a factor of about 0.62: the release switched US devices to miles, which the model, trained on kilometers, read as shorter trips.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: The endpoint's preprocessing converts app 5.2's miles to kilometers; error by version is back to normal.

parts.label: Not retrain
parts.modelAnswer: Retraining on a week of mixed units would teach the model the bug. The attribution was unchanged, so the relationship had not drifted; the input had. The unit is now in the request contract.

bakedIn.headline: Skew is a data bug, not a reason to retrain
bakedIn.body: The world did not change; the input's unit did. Retraining on skewed data teaches the model the bug. Fix the input, then monitor.

scoring.modelReasoning: The skew is on one feature and only for the new app version, whose distances are about 0.62 times the others': miles read as kilometers. The model's reliance on distance has not changed, so this is training-serving skew from a client change, not drift. Fix the serving preprocessing to convert, check error by version, and make the unit part of the contract. Retraining on mixed units bakes the bug in; raising the threshold hides it.
